trace.message: Denied. Wrong service: the problem is in checkout-api.

args.title: checkout-api: elevated error rate and failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 18% with healthy=false while all regions ran v2.3.1.

Action taken: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. v2.3.0 was the most recent release verified healthy in production (prior healthy release v2.2.9). Rollback completed and verified; all three regions now report version v2.3.0.

Notes: v2.3.1 remains marked unhealthy in release history and v2.3.1-c was an unhealthy staging build, so neither was used as a rollback target. Next steps: confirm error rate returns to baseline in all regions, then root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-deploy.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Investigation**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy=false` and an **18% error rate**.
- Release history showed the most recent production-healthy release was **v2.3.0** (the prior one being v2.2.9). v2.3.1 was unhealthy, and `v2.3.1-c` was an unhealthy *staging* build, so it was not a valid rollback target.

**Rollback**
- Rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** in all production regions. Verified: all three regions now report v2.3.0, `healthy=true`, error rate down to **0.2%**.
- One mid-task error on my part: my first rollback call used an incorrect service name (`checkout-service`) and was correctly denied by the approver — no change was made. The corrected call succeeded.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2 for `checkout-api`, on-call paged. It documents the post-v2.3.1 health check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, and next steps.

**Suggested follow-ups:** root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-deploy, and watch the error rate to confirm it stays at baseline. Note that a re-deploy of v2.3.1 would require change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.
